summary: An integer past 64 bits in a dictionary is read as the nearest real, and implementation-limits/integer-values reads the real. ADR 3393 carried Lexer::integer_out_of_range to the validator for content streams only (Runs::AsWritten); the parser path never asks it. ISO 19005 rule: 6.1.13.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.3 (an integer is a run of digits whatever its length); ISO 19005-2 section 6.1.13 and ISO 19005-4 section 6.1.13 bound integers (paraphrased).
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/lexer.rs:822 (wide_integer set, Token::Real returned); crates/pdf-syntax/src/parser.rs (no read of integer_out_of_range); crates/pdf-archive/src/table/file_structure.rs integer-values
change: Log the class syntax/integer-past-i64 with the object, and map it to integer-values.

summary: An indirect object the reader cannot load — bytes that do not parse, or a table entry whose offset holds another object's header — is cached as Object::Null, the value of an undefined reference. The page's content stream leaves the walk, and the damaged file fails fewer rows than its twin. misfiled_objects records the second case; no row asks it. ISO 19005 rule: 5.1, 6.1.4, every content row.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10 (null is the value of a reference to an object that does not exist, not of one that exists and is damaged); §7.5.4 (the entry's offset is the object's).
change: Log syntax/object-unreadable and syntax/object-misfiled; map both to 5.1 and to the content rows' completeness (a page whose content was lost is not certified).

summary: An indirect object with no endobj is read whole, and file-structure/indirect-object-syntax's end_of_object returns when it finds no keyword to judge — the validator's own tolerance stacked on the reader's. ISO 19005 rule: 6.1.9.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.10 (an indirect object is bracketed by obj and endobj); ISO 19005-2 section 6.1.9 sets the endobj keyword's end-of-line markers (paraphrased).
change: Log syntax/endobj-missing; end_of_object records a finding where the region holds no endobj.

summary: Cross-reference repairs: offsets that miss their objects are followed to the objects without a rebuild or a record; a /Prev chain that loops is rebuilt by scanning (Document::was_recovered). The validator's population is the repaired table and no row asks either. ISO 19005 rule: 5.1, 6.1.4.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.5.4 (each entry's offset is the object's), §7.5.6 (/Prev is the previous section's offset).
change: Log syntax/xref-offset-searched, syntax/xref-rebuilt, syntax/xref-chain-cut, syntax/xref-entries-lost; map to 5.1 (and 6.1.4 where the table's own syntax is the subject).

summary: An embedded TrueType program the reader repaired (head.indexToLocFormat wrong: sfnt::repaired_font_program rewrites the loca format) or could only partly read (cut in half) loads without FontError::Malformed, so program_unparsed and every font row pass it. fonts/font-programs-conform-to-their-own-specifications is Unchecked. ISO 19005 rule: 6.2.11.4.1 / 6.2.10.4.1.
source: ISO 32000-2 §9.9 (the embedded program is the font program in its own format); ISO 19005-2 section 6.2.11.4.1 (the embedded program is what a reader renders, and it defines every glyph used), paraphrased.
change: Log font/sfnt-loca-extent, font/sfnt-loca-format, font/sfnt-loca-order and font/program-truncated; map to font-programs-embedded and the conform row.

summary: Base-standard syntax tolerated with no row: a repeated dictionary key (first kept), an unterminated literal string (runs to the end of the stream), a key that is not a name (skipped). Section 5.1's row is Unchecked, so the verdict is Conforms. ISO 19005 rule: 5.1.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.7: "Multiple entries in the same dictionary shall not have the same key" and every key is a name; §7.3.4.2 (balanced parentheses).
change: Log syntax/duplicate-key, syntax/key-not-a-name, syntax/string-unterminated; section 5.1's row becomes Implemented over the log (ADR 3477).

summary: Page entries of the wrong type or value are substituted: a /MediaBox that is a name (Page::substituted_media_box), a /Rotate of 45 (read as 0). Neither record reaches the validator. ISO 19005 rule: 5.1.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.7.3.3, Table 31 (MediaBox a rectangle; Rotate "shall be a multiple of 90").
change: Log model/media-box-substituted and model/rotate-not-a-multiple; map to 5.1.

summary: Content operators given operands they do not take are repaired by the interpreter (an operator with a wrong-typed operand does nothing; one short of operands is dispatched with what is there; Q with nothing saved is ignored; Tj outside BT is drawn; three sc operands under DeviceGray are read as DeviceRGB). Several are reported to the viewer (Unsupported::OperandShortfall, StreamSyntaxFault::TextOperatorOutsideATextObject); the survey walks tokens and never interprets, so none reaches the validator — and the colour case paints in a space the validator never records. ISO 19005 rule: 5.1, 6.2.4.3.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.2 and the operator tables (Table 58, Table 73), §8.4.2 ("Occurrences of the q and Q operators shall be balanced within a given content stream"), §9.4.1.
change: Either the survey takes the interpreter's Unsupported/StreamSyntaxFault for each page (one walk, ADR 3477's log), or the content reader logs its classes as it tokenises; map to 5.1, and the colour case to 6.2.4.3's rows.

summary: decoded_stream_data drops filter::Damage: every caller of the unreported API (images, xref streams, object streams, ICC profiles, metadata) takes a damaged prefix as a whole decode.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.4 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; Inventory S040, S044 and the xref-stream row; the fix is the channel's first class.

summary: Object-stream and xref-stream losses the existing reports miss: a member that fails to parse is dropped and not added to objects_lost_to_damage; a missing /N reads as 0 with short_by 0; non-integer /Index pairs are dropped and the subsections shift.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.5.8, §7.5.7 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; Silent to the viewer's own reports as well as to the validator.

summary: Font maps read leniently with no record: a damaged ToUnicode keeps the prefix that parsed, an absent and a damaged one are one empty map, a damaged Encoding CMap skips entries, a malformed /W or /W2 stops at the first bad entry, a malformed /Differences is skipped item by item, an /Encoding name outside Table 112 becomes no encoding.
source: ISO 32000-2 §9.7.5, §9.10.3 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; Probed: a damaged ToUnicode on a non-symbolic TrueType font passes (6.2.11.7.2 exempts the font, so 5.1 only).

summary: CFF and Type 1 programs read leniently: an unreadable subroutine INDEX or Private DICT becomes none, a TrueType collection is cut to one face (face 0 where /FontName matches none), a failed hinting instance is dropped.
source: ISO 32000-2 §9.9 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; FontDictRepair is the one CFF repair already recorded.

summary: Interpreter tolerances silent to the viewer's own Unsupported: extra operands before an operator dropped; EMC, EX and BX unbalanced; a BDC /OC naming no property list shows the content; an ExtGState entry of the wrong type ignored and an unparsable transfer function discarded; a form's malformed /Matrix read as identity and /BBox as no clip.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.4.5, §8.10.1, §8.11.3 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; The viewer's report (trap 5) misses these whatever the validator does.

summary: A /P that does not read as an integer becomes 0, which states permissions; a string that cannot be decrypted becomes empty.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4 (the entry's form; cited, not quoted).
change: A class on ADR 3477's channel for each site; PDF/A forbids encryption (6.1.3), so the validator fails such a file anyway; the viewer's silence is the finding.
